title: Mass is never lost
body: In a chemical reaction, atoms aren't created or destroyed. They swap partners to make new substances, so the total mass after a reaction is the same as before.
Baking soda and vinegar react to make carbon dioxide gas. That gas is made of real atoms with real mass: about half the mass of the baking soda ends up as gas.
In a sealed bag the gas is trapped, so the reading stays the same. In an open bag the gas drifts away, and the scale drops by the mass that left.

One honest catch: as a sealed bag swells, it pushes aside air, and that air buoys it up a little, so a very precise balance shows a small drop (about 1.2 g for every litre the bag grows). The mass inside hasn't changed.
realWorld: A sealed can of fizzy drink weighs the same before and after you shake it. Open it, and as the gas escapes it slowly gets lighter, and flatter.
